Here’s a straightforward way to handle this without the app and still be safe.

- On your phone or computer, go to: delta.com

  - Airline: Delta
  - Flight number: DL3391
  - Date: 19 September

- Email:  
  - Subject lines like “Your upcoming trip has changed”, “Important: Flight cancellation”, or “We’ve rebooked you”.  
  - Email will say either “your flight has been cancelled” and/or show a new itinerary if they auto‑rebook you.

- Text message (if they have your mobile on file and you allowed alerts):  
  - Short text like “Delta: Your flight DL3391 on 19SEP has been cancelled. Check your rebooking options …”.

- App push notification (if you use the app and sign in):  
  - Pop‑up saying the flight is delayed, changed, or cancelled, often with a link to rebook.

None of these are 100% guaranteed (depends on what contact info they have), so the manual web check is still important.

- 24 hours before departure:  
  - Go to delta.com → Flight Status → DL3391 (19 Sept).

  - If it’s still “scheduled” or “on time” (even if slightly delayed), you can head to the airport as normal.
